strategy.summary: Reproduce GH#63903 / PR#63925: Series.apply and Series.map on Int64/UInt64 with a missing value route through float64 (via to_numpy), losing precision above 2^53. Build pandas from the buggy commit caa6a62b7cf1 in editable mode, then run the added tests test_apply_nullable_integer_precision and test_map_nullable_integer_precision parametrized over Int64 and UInt64; they should fail on the buggy revision and pass on the fixed revision.

system_packages: a C/C++ compiler toolchain (gcc or clang)
pinned_because: Python 3.14.2 is the reported version from the evidence; no other constraint was stated
NumPy, python-dateutil, tzdata and Cython have no documented constraint and no era ceiling in the evidence, so they are left unpinned (latest compatible) and this choice is inferred, not documented

strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/apply/test_series_apply.py::test_apply_nullable_integer_precision and pandas/tests/series/methods/test_map.py::test_map_nullable_integer_precision, each parametrized over dtype Int64 and UInt64
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision caa6a62b7cf1 the parametrized Int64 and UInt64 cases of both tests fail in tm.assert_series_equal because the result is float64 (or value 10000000000000002 rather than 10000000000000003), so the test fails; on the fixed revision (PR#63925 applied) the same cases pass with the nullable dtype preserved and exact values. The transition is fail-to-pass.
strategy.numerical_probe: ser = pd.Series([10000000000000001, None], dtype='Int64'); ser.apply(lambda x: x + 2 if pd.notna(x) else x).dtype and the first value as int

input_output_examples.input: sequence = [10000000000000001, None]; ser = pd.Series(sequence, dtype='Int64'); result = ser.apply(add_two) where add_two returns pd.NA if pd.isna(x) else x + 2

risks: The PR discussion says it should not be merged as-is pending maintainer decisions on return type (ExtensionArray vs object ndarray) and deprecation, so behaviour under the fix may change; the fail-to-pass transition is anchored to the added tests, not to a final merged API.

The PR diff also modifies pandas/tests/extension/test_masked.py and test_map_empty; the fixed-side pass depends on those, so running only the two new tests is sufficient for the transition but not a full regression check.
The tolerance is null; the added tests use exact assert_series_equal, so no tolerance can rescue the buggy result.

The PR date is blank, so the buggy commit cannot be dated against the report; the reported pandas 3.0.0 / numpy 2.4.1 may not match caa6a62b7cf1 exactly, so confirm the buggy revision actually fails before trusting the transition.

The failure requires a build with the 64-bit integer path and a float64 conversion in BaseMaskedArray.map; it is platform-independent in logic but has not been shown on a specific architecture, and no sanitiser or special platform is implicated in the evidence.
UInt64 with value 10000000000000001 plus 2 stays within uint64 range, so no overflow is expected; the failure mode is precision loss, not wraparound.
